avertissement: Traductions automatiques des textes français ; chaque nombre a été vérifié contre le français. Les documents de la Ville sont en français et font foi.

canopee.description: Tree planting, greening, control of the emerald ash borer and heat islands.
canopee.enBref: The City buys trees and has them planted on public land, and pays an organization to green private and institutional land. Boroughs add their own means: money from park funds, machinery rental, blue-collar crews. Exemptions also govern tree planting in two building projects.

etapes.texte: City council awards contracts to 7574479 Canada inc. and Terrassement Technique Sylvain Labrecque inc. to supply and plant 1,374 trees, then water, maintain and replace some of them. The maximum expense is $2,456,590.55, taxes included, for trees distributed across seven boroughs.

Pierrefonds-Roxboro transfers up to $162,233.12 from its fund reserved for park purposes to the purchase of trees and plants. City council pays $3,071,550 to the Société de verdissement du Montréal métropolitain to plant and maintain trees on private and institutional sites from March 24 to December 31, 2026.

Mercier–Hochelaga-Maisonneuve authorizes an extension at 1620, rue Préfontaine with 25 trees and 5% greening instead of the required 40 trees and 25%. Montréal-Nord allows trees to be planted less than 1.5 metres from the street line at 5745, boulevard Léger, for a two-storey building.

Mercier–Hochelaga-Maisonneuve rents a mini-backhoe loader with operator for $152,916.75, taxes included, and sets aside $200,000 for additional blue-collar crews assigned to planting, from May to November 2026. Outremont entrusts URBEX Construction inc. with the renovation of the parc Pratt chalet and the redevelopment of its surroundings, including plant planting, funded in part by the Programme de réfection et de verdissement des parcs locaux.

City council leases land in the Namur-Hippodrome neighbourhood, in Côte-des-Neiges–Notre-Dame-de-Grâce, to the Société de verdissement du Montréal métropolitain for a total rent of $100 before taxes. The organization stores materials, equipment and trees intended for planting there.

aSurveiller.texte: The Société de verdissement du Montréal métropolitain must submit its accountability report by December 31, 2026 at the latest, then its summary and financial statements by March 31, 2027.
The lease for the Namur-Hippodrome neighbourhood nursery runs until April 30, 2028.

deneigement.description: Snow removal and snow loading contracts, spreading of abrasives, parking by-laws.

etapes.titre: Maintenance and snow removal of public squares
etapes.texte: Ville-Marie awarded companies contracts for snow removal, spreading of abrasives, and maintenance of Square Viger, Place des Montréalaises, square Dorchester, place du Canada, l'îlot Bonaventure, square Victoria, place du Sable-Gris, and square Chaboillez. It also extended the Quartier des Spectacles snow removal contract by one year [CA26 24 0067].

Montréal-Nord approved an additional expense of $106,150.97, taxes included, for renting a grader from November 2025 to April 30, 2026 [CA26 10 086]. Saint-Léonard drew $200,000 from its surpluses for wages and abrasives, and Verdun offered to provide its own staff at its snow disposal site.

aSurveiller.texte: The turnkey snow removal contracts for Côte-des-Neiges–Notre-Dame-de-Grâce, Lachine, Outremont, and Le Sud-Ouest end on April 15, 2030; the one for Le Plateau-Mont-Royal ends on April 15, 2031. Each season runs from November 1 to April 15.
Snow removal for the Grand parc de l'Ouest, in the Anse-à-l'Orme, Bois-de-la-Roche, and Cap-Saint-Jacques sectors, covers November 1, 2026 to April 30, 2028.
Extended towing services for Rosemont–La Petite-Patrie, Ville-Marie, and Villeray–Saint-Michel–Parc-Extension start on November 15, 2026.
Equipment rental with operator in Rosemont–La Petite-Patrie starts on November 1, 2026 and runs until March 31, 2027.

eau-egouts.description: Pipes, drinking water production plants, Jean-R.-Marcotte wastewater treatment plant, retention basins.
eau-egouts.enBref: This year, the City is funding and carrying out work on its water networks: watermains and sewer pipes, replacement of lead service connections, drinking water production plants and the Jean-R.-Marcotte wastewater treatment plant. It is awarding contracts for the reconstruction and rehabilitation of pipes on streets in many boroughs. It is also moving forward the project for ozone disinfection of wastewater discharged into the Saint-Laurent river.

etapes.texte: The City is raising to $381,000,000 the loan that funds the disinfection unit at the Jean-R.-Marcotte wastewater treatment plant. The money is to be used to finish the ozonation unit, install liquid oxygen tanks, and build the oxygen plant.

The City is awarding contracts to rehabilitate secondary water pipes without trenching, redo roadways and sidewalks, and replace lead water service connections. The streets targeted are notably in Pierrefonds-Roxboro, Saint-Laurent, Ahuntsic-Cartierville, Villeray–Saint-Michel–Parc-Extension, Côte-des-Neiges–Notre-Dame-de-Grâce, Le Plateau-Mont-Royal and Mercier–Hochelaga-Maisonneuve.

The City is retaining Pure Technologies ltd. to install fibre optics and continuously monitor 38 kilometres of prestressed concrete main pipes for ten years. City council takes a step toward a $951,000,000 loan by-law for the renewal of secondary waterworks and sewer networks from 2027 to 2031.

aSurveiller.texte: Announced adoption of the $951,000,000 loan by-law for secondary waterworks and sewer networks, on October 19, 2026.
Shutdown of sludge incinerator 4 at the Jean-R.-Marcotte plant in January 2027, for about six weeks of work.
Completion of the rue de la Cathédrale water pipe work pushed back to March 2027.
Rue Guy worksite expected to continue until December 2027.
Commissioning of the ozone plant at the Jean-R.-Marcotte plant expected in 2029; contracts for lots 4, 5 and 6 are to be completed by the last quarter of 2028.

frederic-back.titre: Parc Frédéric-Back and Saint-Michel Environmental Complex
frederic-back.description: The former quarry turned landfill, transformed into a park in phases: urban greenhouses, biogas capture, electrical system rationalization.

etapes.titre: Funding request for an east-west link
etapes.texte: The City is asking the ministère des Transports et de la Mobilité durable du Québec for funding of up to $2,000,000 for a 900-metre multi-use trail crossing the park, with a footbridge of about 150 metres. The project also includes rainwater management structures and a 12.7-hectare meadow.

The urban agglomeration council approves construction of a greenhouse complex, valued at $2,185,000, then assigns its completion to the city council, which awards it to the arrondissement de Villeray–Saint-Michel–Parc-Extension. In July, the borough awards Les industries Harnois inc. a contract of $499,865.92 to supply and install two greenhouses.

The City awards Systèmes Urbains inc. a contract of $1,091,693.37 for the second phase of electrical work at the Complexe environnemental de Saint-Michel. The work includes a new 25 kV supply, a transformer, a backup generator and an automated system to manage biogas capture.

The borough awards Groupe MPotvin the redevelopment of rue De Louvain between the park and boulevard Saint-Michel, for a maximum of $8,199,514.82. The work covers sewers, water mains, lighting, sidewalks, cycling facilities and planting.

Two companies are awarded 30-month contracts for general maintenance and ecological and horticultural management of the park. The City is also extending the rental of a compost screener and a loader tractor by five months, for an additional $296,349.21; the compost is used in particular for park development.
The City is extending by six months the snow removal contract for parc Frédéric-Back, the TAZ and the soccer stadium, awarded to 178001 Canada inc. (Groupe Nicky), for an additional $193,215.49.

aSurveiller.texte: The call for projects under the ministère des Transports' funding program, for the footbridge and east-west link, ends on November 26, 2026.
Installation work on the greenhouses must be completed by December 2026; commissioning is announced for winter 2027.
The Boisé Ouest sector, 26 hectares, is to be added in 2027 to the 65 hectares already open to the public.
The snow removal extension covers the period from November 1, 2026 to April 30, 2027.
The rue De Louvain worksite continues from May to October 2027 (sidewalks, curbs, bumpouts), then from May to August 2028 (final roadway, bike path, planting).

grand-parc-ouest.description: Canada's largest municipal park, being assembled: land acquisitions, Anse-à-l'Orme, Cap-Saint-Jacques, Bois-de-la-Roche, parc-nature des Sources.

etapes.texte: The City is adding $162,897.98, taxes included, to the contract for repairing the heritage walls on chemin de Senneville, bringing the contract to $1,174,331.77, taxes included. The file explains the costs by unforeseen site conditions: buried stones that had to be cleaned by hand, extra mortar, sod, and a deteriorated culvert that needs replacing.

The City is submitting the application for the Cap-Saint-Jacques area (330 hectares) for DarkSky International's international Urban Night Sky Place designation. Submitting the application involves no spending; if the designation is granted, the City commits to producing a lighting plan, bringing its light fixtures up to standard, and keeping the site accessible at night.

etapes.titre: Two areas listed as natural environments
etapes.texte: The parc-nature des Sources (38.32 ha) and the Anse-à-l'Orme sector of the Grand parc de l'Ouest (429 ha) are added to the Répertoire des milieux naturels protégés et contributifs à la biodiversité (Registry of natural environments protected and contributing to biodiversity) of the urban agglomeration, with conservation plans. The 2025 report submitted shows 4,051 ha listed or provisionally listed, or 8.1% of the agglomeration's territory.

A contract worth $366,117.31, taxes included, is awarded to Gendron Gestion Civil inc. to rebuild the culvert under chemin Senneville, as part of modernizing the Bois-de-la-Roche agricultural hub; the total expenditure reaches $481,850.45, taxes included. The undersized culvert had been damaged by the heavy rains of August 2024.

etapes.titre: Snow removal, cleaning, and tree felling
etapes.texte: The City is awarding Paysagiste Solarco inc. the contract for snow removal on service roads and parking lots in the Anse-à-l'Orme, Bois-de-la-Roche, and Cap-Saint-Jacques areas ($178,330.82, taxes included), and awarding 9232-3914 Québec inc. the janitorial maintenance of nine buildings at Cap-Saint-Jacques ($704,619.24, taxes included). Entrepreneur Paysagiste Strathmore (1997) ltée will fell ash trees and other dying trees in the park, for a total expenditure of $1,713,041.27, taxes included.

aSurveiller.texte: Snow removal of service roads and parking lots from November 1, 2026 to April 30, 2028.
Janitorial maintenance of nine Cap-Saint-Jacques buildings from November 1, 2026 to October 31, 2030, with a possible extension to October 31, 2031.
Felling of ash trees and dying trees from fall 2026 to early summer 2028.
Cap-Saint-Jacques lighting management plan to be submitted in February 2027, response from DarkSky International expected in April 2027, full site compliance by April 2032.

itinerance.description: Support for organizations, warming centres and shelters for people experiencing homelessness.
itinerance.enBref: The City lends municipal buildings to organizations to open warming centres, and it funds organizations that work with people experiencing homelessness. It also deploys a Ville-Marie public works team to other boroughs for cleanliness interventions related to homelessness. It is setting up a framework to receive private donations and is appealing a ruling on the encampments under the Van Horne viaduct.

etapes.texte: The City lends three buildings free of charge to organizations for the winter: the church at 5600, 12e Avenue to the Centre des Femmes de convictions de Montréal, the former Recluses Missionaries monastery at 12050, boulevard Gouin Est to Projets Autochtones du Québec, and the Bain St-Denis at 7075, rue Saint-Hubert to L'Amour en Action SYL DAN. The loans end on April 30, 2026 and the value of the unbilled rent is estimated at $57,076 for the church.

Verdun pays $12,950 to the Société de développement social to keep community outreach workers in its municipal facilities from January 5 to February 6, 2026. Ahuntsic-Cartierville ratifies the continuation of the contract with Les services de cohabitation sociale COHAB inc. for a warming centre for the 2025-2026 winter.

The City grants financial support to community organizations under the Programme itinérance et milieux inclusifs 2026-2028, for inclusion, public space cohabitation and awareness projects. The amounts cover a three-year period ending on December 31, 2028.

etapes.titre: Private donations and fit-up of the Bain St-Denis
etapes.texte: City council adopts a framework to receive private donations intended for housing, shelter and social cohabitation projects; donors do not choose which project is funded. Rosemont–La Petite-Patrie transfers $250,000 for the activities and fit-up work of the temporary warming centre at the Bain Saint-Denis. City council also adopts a declaration of support for people experiencing homelessness and a motion on a rent support fund.

etapes.titre: Encampments on rue Notre-Dame and appeal proceedings
etapes.texte: The City awards a contract worth $149,520, taxes included, to Mission Old Brewery to help people from the rue Notre-Dame encampment area move toward shelter and housing, and pays $90,000 to the Réseau d'aide aux personnes seules et itinérantes de Montréal for the 2026, 2027 and 2028 editions of the Nuit des sans-abri. The executive committee takes charge of the dispute over the encampments under the Van Horne viaduct and authorizes an appeal of the June 8, 2026 ruling.

aSurveiller.texte: Mission Old Brewery's mandate in the rue Notre-Dame encampment area ends on October 18, 2026.
The agreement between Ville-Marie and Rivière-des-Prairies–Pointe-aux-Trembles for the public works team runs until May 15, 2027.
Support under the Programme itinérance et milieux inclusifs ends on December 31, 2028.

louvain-est.description: The neighbourhood being built on municipal land in Ahuntsic-Cartierville: acquisitions, soil decontamination, street names, temporary developments.

etapes.texte: The City is extending the rental of a lot to the Société de transport de Montréal for parking of its agents' vehicles, south of rue de Louvain and west of boulevard Saint-Laurent. It is also extending the rental of a neighbouring lot to a company for paid parking reserved for app members.

The Villeray–Saint-Michel–Parc-Extension borough is awarding a company the redevelopment of rue de Louvain, between parc Frédéric-Back and boulevard Saint-Michel. The work covers sewers, water mains, lighting, traffic lights, sidewalks, the bike path and plantings.

etapes.titre: Main street becomes avenue des Solidarités
etapes.texte: City council is naming the new street at the heart of the eco-district "avenue des Solidarités." The name came from a public call for proposals held in fall 2024.

The City is awarding a contract to build a road with sewer, water main, roadway, electrical network and lighting in the eco-district, as well as for environmental soil management. It is adding $2,007,312.15 net, from the environmental liability reserve, to rehabilitate the soil of the former gas station area on the Louvain Est lot.

The borough is adopting a draft resolution authorizing the demolition of a building on avenue de l'Esplanade and rue de Louvain Ouest, followed by the construction of a building complex with a minimum density of 200 dwellings per hectare. It is also launching a draft by-law to increase the height and density allowed on part of the municipal lot at 50 and 150, rue de Louvain Ouest.

aSurveiller.texte: The lease for the lot rented to the Société de transport de Montréal for parking starts on October 1, 2026, for three years, at a rate of 92 days per year.
The free loan of the lot for planting sunflowers and the greenhouse runs from November 1, 2026 to October 31, 2027.
The free loan of the community garden lot continues until December 31, 2027.
The lot at the corner of rue de Louvain Ouest and avenue de l'Esplanade would be loaned for activity programming from April 1 to October 31, 2027.

Work on rue de Louvain between parc Frédéric-Back and boulevard Saint-Michel continues from May to October 2027 (sidewalks, curbs, bump-outs), then from May to August 2028 (final roadway, bike path, plantings).
The street naming file indicates that site developments are planned for around 2032 and that four other public places remain to be named.

matieres-residuelles.description: Collections, sorting centres, biomethanization and ecocentres.
matieres-residuelles.enBref: This year, the City is changing collection days, sectors and frequency in several boroughs, and buying bins for residents. It is extending its food waste processing contracts and its ecocentre-related contracts, and awarding a contract to recover mattresses. It is also tabling the agglomeration's 2025 residual materials management report.

etapes.texte: The City is extending its contracts with Recyclage Notre-Dame inc. twice, by six months each time, to compost or biomethanize food waste from the eastern part of the agglomeration. The materials are transferred in Montréal-Est and then processed in Saint-Thomas-de-Joliette and in Moose Creek, Ontario, until the Montréal-Est organic materials treatment centre comes into service.

etapes.titre: Bin purchases and loan of sorting equipment
etapes.texte: City council enters into agreements with Orbis Canada and USD Global to supply collection bins to residents of the boroughs, then with Plasti-Bac inc. for garbage bins intended for Ahuntsic-Cartierville and Villeray–Saint-Michel–Parc-Extension. The executive committee approves an agreement with Tricentris, which pays $43,773.61, taxes included, for a program lending reusable dishware, water fountains and sorting stations for neighbourhood events.

etapes.titre: Containers, ecocentres and former dump sites
etapes.texte: The agglomeration is extending the collection contracts for garbage from front-load and semi-underground containers, as well as the container contract for the écocentre Saint-Laurent. It is awarding Recyc-Matelas inc. a contract worth $734,690.25, taxes included, to collect and recover mattresses and box springs from ecocentres, assigning two firms studies on constructions located on former waste disposal sites, and extending the contract for the software that manages dumping authorizations.

aSurveiller.texte: The program lending dishware, water fountains and sorting stations is offered until December 31, 2026 at the latest.
The extension of the food waste processing contracts runs until February 28, 2027.
The container contract for the écocentre Saint-Laurent and the container collection contracts are extended until October 31, 2027.
The contract for the dumping authorization management software covers the period from October 12, 2026 to October 11, 2029.

namur-hippodrome.description: The new neighbourhood on the site of the former Blue Bonnets racetrack: sale of land, loan by-laws, waterworks for the Namur–De la Savane sector.
namur-hippodrome.enBref: The City is preparing the future neighbourhood on the site of the former Blue Bonnets racetrack, in Côte-des-Neiges–Notre-Dame-de-Grâce. It obtained an extended deadline from Québec to sell a first piece of land, adopted two loan by-laws for waterworks and public domain works, and transferred a piece of land to an organization for non-market housing. At the same time, it is leasing parcels of the site to organizations for temporary uses.

etapes.titre: Deadline extended to sell a first piece of land
etapes.texte: The Québec government grants the City a deadline until October 31, 2027 to sell a first piece of land on the site of the former racetrack, west of boulevard Décarie and south of rue Paré. The extension involves no financial compensation, and the other conditions of the 2017 transfer deed remain the same.

City council approves a City guarantee of $2,000,000 in favour of the Canada Infrastructure Bank, for a loan to Société GALOPH used to pay for feasibility studies for the residential project. The same day, council rejects a motion from the Official Opposition on governance and the management of public assets and funds in the development of the neighbourhood.

The City borrows $29,000,000 to develop the neighbourhood's public domain: soil remediation, sewers and waterworks, street redevelopment, professional fees and land purchases. It also borrows $12,000,000 to build main waterworks pipes between boulevard Cavendish, in Saint-Laurent, and rue Isabella, in Côte-des-Neiges–Notre-Dame-de-Grâce.

etapes.titre: Four buildings authorized on rue Namur
etapes.texte: The borough of Côte-des-Neiges–Notre-Dame-de-Grâce adopts a draft resolution authorizing the construction of four residential buildings in four phases, at 7301 boulevard Décarie and at 5150-5160 rue Namur. One of the buildings must house a municipal sports and leisure centre, and the developer must pay $3,200,000 for public amenities and equipment in the sector.

The City leases parcels of the site to the community cafeteria MultiCaf and to the Coopérative de solidarité Polliflora for temporary urban agriculture, as well as to the Société de verdissement du Montréal métropolitain for a transitional nursery. Each lease provides for a nominal rent, and the organizations pay for development, maintenance and property taxes.

aSurveiller.texte: Deadline granted by the Québec government to sell a first piece of land on the site: October 31, 2027.
The $128.3M federal grant is conditional on the infrastructure being completed by 2031; the funds from the $29,000,000 loan cover work from 2026 to 2028.
Communia has five years after the signing of the transfer deed to complete at least one building, and housing affordability must last at least 25 years.
End of the temporary leases: April 30, 2027 for MultiCaf, March 31, 2028 for Polliflora and April 30, 2028 for the transitional nursery.

parcs.description: Development and renovation of parks, including the Grand parc de l'Ouest.
parcs.enBref: The City is designing and redoing parks in several boroughs: soil studies, work contracts, public art and adjustments to projects already underway. In the Grand parc de l'Ouest, it is having walls and a culvert repaired, submitting a candidacy for a designation related to the night sky, and awarding snow removal, cleaning and tree felling contracts to companies. Several projects are funded by the participatory budget, the environmental liability reserve or park funds.

etapes.titre: Design, soil studies and funding agreement
etapes.texte: The City awards the design of the Caroline-Dawson library and the redevelopment of parc Le Prévost to a team that won a competition, for a total expenditure of $10,559,257.81 including taxes. It also pays $174,471.56 to Verdun for studies before redoing parc Monseigneur-J.-A.-Richard, and the Sud-Ouest signs an agreement with Hydro-Québec to get $154,000 for parc d'Argenson.

etapes.titre: Grand parc de l'Ouest: work and protection
etapes.texte: The City adds $162,897.98 to the contract to repair the heritage walls on chemin de Senneville and awards a contract to rebuild the culvert under that same road, in the Bois-de-la-Roche agricultural hub. It submits the candidacy of the Cap-Saint-Jacques sector for the Urban Night Sky Place designation and lists the Anse-à-l'Orme sector, along with the parc-nature des Sources, in the directory of protected natural environments.

The City adds $153,434.14 for the supervision of work at parc du Bassin-à-Bois and $168,472.14 to decontaminate parc George-Vernot. The boroughs move or increase budgets for parc des Hirondelles, parc du Sault-au-Récollet, parc Villeray and parc Percy-Walters.

etapes.titre: Maintenance of the Grand parc de l'Ouest
etapes.texte: The agglomeration awards contracts for snow removal on service roads and parking lots in the Anse-à-l'Orme, Bois-de-la-Roche and Cap-Saint-Jacques sectors, for cleaning of nine buildings at Cap-Saint-Jacques, and for felling ash trees and dying trees.

aSurveiller.texte: Selection of the winning public art project for parc des Eaux-Cachées in October 2026, contract with the artist in December 2026 and installation of the work in 2028.
Adoption expected at city council on October 19, 2026, to transfer a 75.2 m² laneway strip to parc Le Prévost.
Start of snow removal and cleaning contracts for the Grand parc de l'Ouest on November 1, 2026.
Response from DarkSky International expected in April 2027 for Cap-Saint-Jacques, with the lighting plan to be submitted in February 2027.
Final acceptance of the work at parc du Bassin-à-Bois expected in June 2027.
End of work at parc J.O.R.-Leduc expected in June 2028.

pietonnisation.description: Pedestrian streets, public squares and by-laws for commercial activities.
pietonnisation.enBref: This year, the City is funding and regulating temporary pedestrian streets on commercial arteries, mainly for the 2026 summer season. The executive committee paid $2,694,500 to the boroughs under the call for projects for pedestrianization on commercial arteries [CE26 0465], and the boroughs adopted the by-laws that close streets and authorize terraces, sales, and music. Other decisions concern public squares: development, change of status of a lot, and an official name.

etapes.titre: Subsidy rules and settlement of a dispute
etapes.texte: Ville-Marie adopts a by-law that allows it to subsidize its commercial development corporations to pedestrianize streets, up to $425 per linear metre, on condition that council closes the street by ordinance [CA26 240037]. Rosemont–La Petite-Patrie settles out of court for $41,686.46 a lawsuit related to work on the public square at the corner of rue Beaubien Est and rue Boyer [CA26 26 0010].

The executive committee distributes $2,694,500 among boroughs for pedestrian streets closed for at least eight consecutive weeks, including rue Villeray as a new project [CE26 0465]. Côte-des-Neiges–Notre-Dame-de-Grâce creates the Placette CDN from April 1 to October 31, 2026 [CA26 170058], and Ville-Marie bans traffic on the sections of its summer pedestrianizations [CA26 240090].

The boroughs pay contributions to the commercial development corporations that organize the pedestrian streets: $102,045 for rue Villeray [CA26 14 0078], $375,500 for rue Sainte-Catherine Est [CA26 240134], and $67,500 for avenue Lacombe until 2028 [CA26 170108]. Outremont allocates $105,000 to the pedestrianization of avenue Bernard, in addition to a $106,000 grant from the Service du développement économique [CA26 16 0061].

The borough councils close their arteries to cars and regulate terraces, sales, and noise: avenue Bernard from May 19 to September 24 [CA26 16 0082], avenues Royal and Madison from June 1 to October 31 [CA26 170088], rue Ontario Est from June 15 to September 18 [CA26 27 0115], avenues du Mont-Royal and Duluth [CA26 25 0134]. Ville-Marie adjusts the dates of three pedestrianizations [CA26 240155], and Mercier–Hochelaga-Maisonneuve removes 113 paid parking spaces [CA26 27 0119].

etapes.titre: Public squares and end of season
etapes.texte: City council changes the status of an 899-square-metre lot at the corner of rue Sherbrooke Est and boulevard Langelier from street (public square) to local park [CM26 0888] and names "place Chez-Marguerite" the public square at the corner of rue Charleroi and avenue L'Archevêque [CM26 0913]. Ville-Marie authorizes sound ambience on the pedestrian streets of the Quartier des spectacles [CA26 240372], and Le Plateau-Mont-Royal revises the reopening schedule for avenue du Mont-Royal [CA26 25 227].

aSurveiller.texte: Avenue du Mont-Royal reopens to traffic between Saint-Denis and Resther on September 30, 2026, and between Saint-Laurent and Saint-Denis on October 15, 2026.
The boroughs must report on the amounts received for pedestrianizations in November 2026 and return any unspent money in December 2026.
The by-law on sound ambience for the pedestrian streets of the Quartier des spectacles runs until September 2, 2027.
The on-demand transit contract for avenue du Mont-Royal covers until December 31, 2027, and support for the pedestrianization of avenue Lacombe until December 31, 2028.

plan-urbanisme.description: The PUM and the concordance by-laws that each borough adopts to comply with it.

etapes.texte: Ahuntsic-Cartierville amends its urban planning by-law for the planting, maintenance, protection and felling of trees. Rosemont–La Petite-Patrie revises its urban planning, special projects and demolition by-laws, and Saint-Léonard does the same for its special projects and demolitions, after public consultations held on February 26 and February 11, 2026.

The borough extends its list of buildings of heritage interest, regulates housing and service establishments for people in situations of residential instability, and amends its by-laws on demolition, special projects and site planning and architectural integration plans. A public assembly was held on March 18, 2026 and a written consultation from March 11 to 18, 2026.

The borough changes the heights, uses and lot occupancy ratio in the sector bounded by avenue Papineau, avenue Émile-Journault, avenue André-Grasset and rue Legendre Est. It also increases the permitted heights on sections of rue Lajeunesse, between boulevard Crémazie and boulevard Henri-Bourassa.

etapes.titre: Requests for extensions to the ministry
etapes.texte: Ahuntsic-Cartierville requests twelve more months, until June 16, 2027, to adopt its concordance by-laws. L'Île-Bizard–Sainte-Geneviève requests six more months, citing lack of staff, the complexity of its territory and the fall 2025 election.

Ville-Marie amends its urban planning by-law and its by-laws on special projects, demolition, authorization certificates and cadastral operations. After the public consultation of March 25, 2026, the City revised the view corridor and height plans; the by-law allows a maximum height of 103 m on the block of the former terrasse Peel and requires approval for certain work in the declared heritage site of the Mont-Royal.

Saint-Léonard takes note of two correction minutes signed on March 19, 2026, which correct the name of a school and the identification of a building on boulevard Provencher. Ahuntsic-Cartierville then adopts its by-law on the demolition of buildings, after a public consultation assembly held on June 23, 2026.

aSurveiller.texte: L'Île-Bizard–Sainte-Geneviève states it wants to present its project to elected officials starting mid-June 2026 and hold a public consultation in September or October 2026.

The Minister of Municipal Affairs has set June 16, 2027 as the deadline for Saint-Léonard to adopt all its concordance by-laws; other blocks have been announced, including the replacement of the zoning by-law.
Ahuntsic-Cartierville requests an extension until June 16, 2027 to adopt its concordance by-laws.
Villeray–Saint-Michel–Parc-Extension has until June 17, 2027 to update its by-laws; its zoning by-law must be replaced in 2027.

securite-publique.description: The Ville de Montréal's police department (Service de police de la Ville de Montréal): contracts, neighbourhood stations, council motions.

etapes.titre: Loan for equipment and loan of an officer
etapes.texte: The urban agglomeration council adopts a by-law authorizing a loan of $10,880,000 to buy and replace specialized SPVM equipment between 2026 and 2030. It also authorizes the loan of a detective sergeant to the RCMP team that enforces the Firearms Act, for three years starting January 7, 2026.

The City buys 11 patrol motorcycles, extends the housekeeping service at headquarters by one year, and awards work to replace the oil heating system of the cavalry building, at 1515 chemin Remembrance. It also awards a contract for meals for detained persons and extends maintenance of the call dispatch system software.

The City leases 50 parking spaces at 260 boulevard De Maisonneuve for headquarters vehicles. It renews the leases for the training centre in Anjou, neighbourhood station 15 in Verdun, and neighbourhood station 26 on avenue Mountain Sights.

The City concludes an agreement to supply 9 mm practice ammunition used for police firearms training, and extends the SPVM's mail pickup and delivery service by one year. It also retains suppliers for carpentry and painting services in the department's buildings.

aSurveiller.texte: "Fèves au lard" fundraising day at neighbourhood station 46, on October 23, 2026; the Anjou borough buys 62 tickets.
The harbour patrol boat and its trailer must be delivered no later than March 1, 2027.
The lease for the metro unit premises of neighbourhood station 50, at 888 boulevard De Maisonneuve Est, starts on February 1, 2027.
The ACCES Tabac, Alcool, Cannabis and ACCEF committees are extended until March 31, 2027.
The work to replace the oil heating system of the cavalry building must be completed by September 30, 2027.

transport-collectif.description: What the City decides around the network: land sold to the STM, areas around stations, agreements.

velo.titre: Bike: REV, bike paths and BIXI
velo.description: The Réseau express vélo, bike paths and bike lanes, and the self-serve bike system.
velo.enBref: This year, the City mainly bought equipment for the BIXI self-serve bike system, paid for work on existing bike lanes, and settled the occupancy of Hydro-Québec land crossed by bike paths. Boroughs awarded maintenance and development contracts, and the City asked Québec for money for four new bike infrastructure projects.

etapes.texte: Rosemont–La Petite-Patrie issued an ordinance that formalizes the bike lanes on avenue Christophe-Colomb between rue des Carrières and rue de Bellechasse and requires mandatory manoeuvres for motorists up to Jean-Talon Est. Outremont authorized $100,000 for deicing salt and abrasives to be spread, notably on its bike paths.

etapes.titre: Bike path repairs and sustainable mobility corridors
etapes.texte: City council added $3,400,000 to the contract with Bruneau Électrique inc. for sustainable mobility corridors in Ville-Marie and Mercier–Hochelaga-Maisonneuve, then approved Ville-Marie and Villeray–Saint-Michel–Parc-Extension carrying out roadway and bike lane work, including repairs to the REV Lajeunesse between Jarry and Crémazie. Ahuntsic-Cartierville retained Déneigement et Excavation M. Gauthier inc. for spring cleaning of narrow bike paths.

City council awarded a sole-source contract of $4,815,802.61 to PBSC Solutions Urbaines inc. for bikes, stations and docking points compatible with the BIXI system. The executive committee then retained Laser AMP, a division of ISE Métal inc., for $394,851.17, to supply the steel pavers that serve as the base for the stations.

Outremont tabled a draft by-law to convert the shared lane on avenue Lajoie, between Stuart and Outremont, into a one-way bike path. Le Plateau-Mont-Royal awarded Cojalac inc. work on rue Parthenais including a BIXI station, and the Sud-Ouest awarded Groupe Damex inc. the development of three green alleys and the electrical installation of a BIXI station.

etapes.titre: Requests for financial assistance from Québec
etapes.texte: City council authorized the submission of four financial assistance requests to the ministère des Transports et de la Mobilité durable, for bike lanes and sidewalks on rue de Champlain, rue Saint-Jacques, rue Guy and rue Laurier. The City commits to paying at least half of the eligible expenses.

aSurveiller.texte: October 9, 2026: deadline to submit complete financial assistance requests to the ministère des Transports et de la Mobilité durable.
The repair of the bike path on rue De Louvain, between west of rue d'Iberville and boulevard Saint-Michel, is budgeted at $570,000 in 2027.
